thread:
marina (secops): Heads-up: we identified a high-severity container escape vector affecting our Dedicated inference hosts that can be mitigated by enforcing a stricter seccomp baseline + two kernel tunables. Immediate action required for Dedicated clusters; Private customers get a configurable opt-in path. Read below for the plan and steps.

ton y (eng-runtime): Thanks — quick Q: is this an runc/CVE issue or a kernel bug?

marina (secops): Root cause is a combination of a runc namespace handling issue and an unprivileged BPF/kprobes vector on kernels < 5.15 with certain config flags. We can block the exploit surface with seccomp + disable unprivileged bpf and unprivileged_userns in sysctl.

karen (eng-sre): TL;DR action items for Dedicated team: 1) Apply new seccomp profile to inference worker pods; 2) Set kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1; 3) Set kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0; 4) Restart affected pods (rolling). Target: 72 hours.

devon (eng-platform): Patch is ready in the infra repo: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/refs/heads/seccomp-hardening. It includes the policy and a DaemonSet that applies the profile via admission webhook.

marina (secops): Commands for immediate remediation (run on node pool control plane or via SRE playbook):

```
# sysctl changes (apply to all Dedicated host VMs)
sudo sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1
sudo sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0
# persist
echo 'kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.d/99-secops.conf
echo 'kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.d/99-secops.conf
sudo sysctl --system
```

And the seccomp profile is in the infra repo under `policies/seccomp/rl-inference-profile.json`. Admission webhook will start rejecting pods that request CAP_SYS_ADMIN or unconfined seccomp.

tony (eng-runtime): Note: some of our older inference containers request CAP_SYS_ADMIN for _legacy_ GPU setup. We need a migration path for those images — set a CPU/GPU init container shim until images are rebuilt. I'll list affected images in the runtime repo.

karen (eng-sre): Rollout schedule: Dedicated pools (priority) -> 72h window. Non-production clusters -> next 24h. Production Dedicated -> staged across regions with canary (5% nodes) then full. Private customers: we'll provide the policy and a patch script; they have 7 days to opt in or request exception.

marina (secops): Exceptions: If you require CAP_SYS_ADMIN for an approved reason, open a ticket in #eng-security with the subject: "seccomp-exception: <team> - <reason>". Include: justification, compensating controls, and ETA to remove. Exceptions are timeboxed (max 14 days) and require CTO approval.

alex (oncall): Deploy bot started a canary: deploy-bot: [deploy] seccomp-hardening canary -> infra-canary-us-west-2 (id: cb-57). Logs show two pods rejected due to unconfined seccomp: `InferenceWorker:v0.9` and `legacy-gpu-init:v2019`.

tony (eng-runtime): I've filed PRs to remove unconfined seccomp from the runtime images and to split the legacy GPU init: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/412. Will tag owners.

marina (secops): Checklist for teams owning Dedicated workloads:
- Pull infra/seccomp profile and test locally (minikube/k3s)
- Ensure no pod requests CAP_SYS_ADMIN or unconfined seccomp
- If needed, switch to the provided shim init container
- Validate with `kubectl create --dry-run=server -f <pod.yaml>` and check audit logs

karen (eng-sre): Quick sanity commands for pod owners:
```
kubectl get pods -o=jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" -> "}{.spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type}{"
"}{end}' -n <namespace>
# find pods requesting elevated caps
kubectl get pods -o=jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" -> "}{.spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities.add}{"
"}{end}' -n <namespace>
```

devon (eng-platform): We'll create a dashboard in Console to show "seccomp rejections" and nodes with sysctl flags not set. Expect ETA 12 hours.

marina (secops): Communication plan: - Email to Dedicated customers with details + private deployment guidance - Post FAQ in #product-security - Weekly follow-up in infra sync until closed.

tony (eng-runtime): Anything that breaks CI or E2E tests because of the policy, ping me immediately. We'll allow a grace flag in test clusters for 48 hours.

marina (secops): Summary and SLA: This is high severity; apply kernel tunables and seccomp baseline within 72 hours for Dedicated. For Private, apply or schedule opt-in within 7 days. Non-compliance will trigger temporary workload throttling to reduce attack surface.

alex (oncall): I'm coordinating the rolling restarts; uptime impact should be low but plan for ~1-2 minute restarts per pod.

marina (secops): Thank you all. I'll keep this thread updated with canary metrics and the master checklist. If you hit any blockers, mention @marina and @karen. :lock:
